ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a vertical wall, and a horizontal rod extends to the right from the point labeled 2 on the wall. Near the middle of the rod is marked point 3, and near the right end is marked point 4. An upward-slanting rope is connected from near the right end of the rod to the higher point labeled 1 on the wall. Reasoning: It is required to select the point for writing the torque equation, so that the force of the rope can be found with only one equation. If the point 2 where the wall and the rod are connected is taken as the pivot, the lines of action of the unknown support reaction forces of the wall on the rod pass through point 2, so the torques of these unknown reaction forces are zero and will be eliminated from the torque equation. The weight of the rod acts near the middle, and the tension of the rope acts near the right end; they still have moment arms about point 2, so one torque equilibrium equation can be used to find the rope tension. Therefore point 2 should be selected.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a horizontal uniform rod attached to the wall at labeled point 2, with its weight acting at the rod’s center near point 3 and a supporting rope running from the upper wall point 1 to the rod’s right end near point 4. From the text, the goal is to choose a torque point so that one torque equation can solve for the rope force. Use the rule that taking torques about the point where unknown support/contact forces act makes those forces produce zero torque. Since the wall/hinge force on the rod acts at point 2, choose point 2; then the unknown wall reaction drops out, while the rope force and the rod’s weight still have nonzero moment arms, giving a single equation for the rope force.

method.method_draft: First inspect the labeled points in the diagram: point 1 lies on the rope’s wall attachment, point 4 lies near the rope’s attachment to the rod, point 3 is near the rod’s center, and point 2 is the wall support of the rod. From the text, the pivot should allow solving for rope force, so the rope force must not be eliminated, while other unknown forces should be eliminated. Test the candidates: about point 1 or point 4, the rope’s line of action passes through the pivot, so the rope torque is zero and the rope force cannot be solved. About point 3, the rod’s weight is eliminated but the wall reaction at point 2 remains unknown, so not a single-equation solution. About point 2, the wall reaction torque is zero, but the rope and weight torques remain, so the rope force can be found from one torque balance. Therefore choose point 2.
